description: Verdict of the safety gate on every rewrite this project has recorded as ACCEPTED, keyed by FNV-1a of source+replacement. Meaning lives in accepted-labels.json and never changes; this file is the moving record of what the gate does. `history` records every CHANGED rewrite a re-baseline has closed and every PRESERVING one it has given up, so neither can happen quietly. Regenerate with `node bench/precision-check.mjs --write --note "why"`.

history.note: Initial snapshot, taken with the hand labelling of all 274 recorded accepted rewrites. 8 CHANGED rows are accepted today and stand as the defect list this round works.

Closed three distinguishing-modifier/head-noun defects by comparing related-word COUNTS instead of asking whether any related survivor exists. Pro-form and discourse-connective exemptions keep the two legitimate cases that rule would otherwise have refused; 'process' moved from a blanket stock noun to the 'in the process of' frame.

fixed.from: There was evidence that during the breakup sequence, the right Solid Rocket Booster struck the outboard end of the Orbiter's right wing and right outboard elevon.
fixed.to: There was evidence that the Solid Rocket Booster struck the Orbiter's right wing and right outboard elevon during the breakup sequence.

fixed.from: The spacecraft body structure consists of a payload structure and a spacecraft structure.
fixed.to: The spacecraft body structure consists of a payload structure and a structure.

fixed.from: She summarised the briefest possible summary of the fault.
fixed.to: She summarized the briefest possible fault.

history.note: Closed two lone-edit defects: a word introduced from inside a protected token (the literal fallback in vocabularyHasAntecedent read the raw source), and a lone derivational swap treated as an inflection (bonding -> bond). Neither cost anything on the oracle or the unlock control.

fixed.from: on tuesday the electrician tested the bonding.
fixed.to: On Tuesday the electrician tested the bond.

fixed.from: Read the notes in /srv/reports/audit.md before the meeting.
fixed.to: Read the audit notes in /srv/reports/audit.md before the meeting.

history.note: Closed the deadline-preposition defect: 'before Thursday' -> 'by Thursday' moved a boundary that no guard was watching, because both words are function words and nothing else changed.

fixed.from: Could you send the revised drawings before Thursday?
fixed.to: Could you send the revised drawings by Thursday?

history.note: Closed the agentless-passive defect: an active verb replaced by 'be' plus its own past participle moves the subject from agent to patient, and rolesFlipped cannot see it because there is no by-phrase to compare.

fixed.from: Will the parts clear inspection before Friday?
fixed.to: Will the parts be cleared for inspection before Friday?

history.note: Recall regained on 'at the present time': the stock-phrase list excused 'time' and not 'present', so deleting the phrase outright was billed for half of itself. Found by running the development corpus against a live llama-server, which is also what added the recall-gain line to this report.

recallRegained.from: The current policy remains active at the present time.

history.note: Extended for the row the first live end-to-end run added (an expletive unpacking, PRESERVING).
The conjunct guard refuses a dissolved coordination outright instead of deferring it: 'a smaller and more reliable component' -> 'a smaller component'. Costs one Grammarly row, named in the commit.

Corrected a miscount, not a regression: the inversion rule counted failure words per diff RUN, so 'documented the failure in the incident log' -> 'documented the incident log failure' was reported as losing a word that is still in the sentence, and deferred to the verifier on that false premise. The verifier showed it, so the rewrite reached the writer before this change and after it; what changed is that the precision control now counts it honestly as a standing defect instead of filing it under the verifier. A content-reorder guard that would catch it was tried and rejected: it cost 8 oracle rows and 2 preserving rewrites to catch this one.
dropsRepeatedWord: a lost word the sentence still contains, only fewer times, is refused outright rather than deferred. Free on all three instruments.
deadlineNarrowed: a deadline phrase that kept its preposition and its time but lost the words between them is refused outright. Free on all three instruments.
subordinatorReattached closes the conditional re-attachment defect. Free on all three instruments.

fixed.from: Wanted to flag a risk early, if the API rate limits kick in during peak hours the whole checkout flow could stall.
fixed.to: Wanted to flag a risk early if the API rate limits kick in during peak hours, as the whole checkout flow could stall.

history.note: objectAdjunctCompounded: a verb's object and its locative phrase folded into one compound is order-changed; closes the adjunct-reanalysed row at no recall cost

fixed.from: Ravi documented the failure in the incident log.
fixed.to: Ravi documented the incident log failure.

history.note: topicComplementObjectified: closes the determination-regarding row at no recall cost; one CHANGED row (loose/loosening) still left to the verifier

confusableResolvedByDerivation: closes the loose/loosening row at no recall cost. Zero CHANGED rows now reach the writer, outright or through the verifier. classify() now also counts a verifier-deferred CHANGED row that becomes an outright refusal as closed; the earlier entries that did the same (conjunct, repeated-word, deadline, topic-complement) predate that and show fixed:0 in this history.

fixed.to: Make sure you loosen the bolts before loosening the alignment.

history.note: reason merge: dropped-content folded into content-dropped (gate fix 1.4f); no decision changed

Phase 3.2 re-measurement: holdouts 1-3 re-run on the pinned b10760 binary and the pinned Q6_K in the shipped tier configuration, plus three attribution runs in the old configuration.
